description:
Browser API Client is a lightweight API testing tool that lives in your browser. No desktop app to install, no account to create, no cloud sync you didn't ask for. Click the toolbar button and a full-tab workspace opens: build a request, hit Send. Nothing is lost when you click away.

FEATURES (free, no limits):
- Full HTTP support — GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS.
- Request builder — URL bar synced with query params, headers, and bodies: JSON, URL-encoded form, multipart with files, raw text, binary file.
- Authentication — Bearer token, Basic auth, API key (header or query), and OAuth 2.0: client credentials, or authorization code with PKCE. Tokens stay on your device and refresh automatically.
- Response viewer — Status, timing, size, the full redirect chain and Set-Cookie headers. Failures are named: DNS, refused connection, TLS certificate, timeout. Pretty JSON and a collapsible tree, raw body, search, image and sandboxed HTML preview, binary hex view and download.
- Tests without scripts — check status, headers, JSON paths, body text and response time on every response, and pull values into variables to chain requests.
- Collection runner — run a collection or folder in order, see pass/fail for every request, re-run just the failures.
- GraphQL and Server-Sent Events — a GraphQL body editor with variables, and event streams shown live as they arrive.
- Code snippets — cURL, JavaScript fetch, Node axios, Python requests, Go, PHP, C# and HTTPie, with values from the active environment.
- Unlimited request history — grouped by day, searchable, filter by method or status, reopen in one click.
- Multiple environments — switch between dev, staging, and production with one click. {{variables}} are highlighted as you type, undefined ones are flagged before you send, and secret values are masked.
- Collections — save with Cmd/Ctrl+S into collections and folders. Search, rename, duplicate, reorder by drag or keyboard.
- Import — paste a cURL command, an OpenAPI 3 or Swagger 2 spec, a Postman v2.1 collection or environment, or a HAR file. Export collections back to Postman. No lock-in.
- Dark and light themes.

WHY BROWSER API CLIENT?
- Postman killed its free team plan. API testing shouldn't require a subscription to a bloated desktop app.
- Thunder Client, REST Client — they live in VS Code. This lives in your browser, where you're already looking at the API docs.
- Zero tracking. Zero analytics. Your API keys and tokens stay on your device.
- Requests execute via the extension's background worker, bypassing CORS. Test any API from any page.

Built by Brightbar (brightbar.dev).
single_purpose: Send HTTP requests to any API endpoint and inspect the responses, with request history, environment variables, saved collections, import from cURL/OpenAPI/Postman/HAR and code snippet export.

permission_justifications.storage: Used to save request history, environment variables, collections, and user preferences (theme, history limit) locally on the user's device. All data stays on the device.
permission_justifications.host_permissions: Core functionality. The extension sends HTTP requests to API endpoints specified by the user. Since developers need to test APIs on any domain, broad host permission is required. Requests are only sent when the user explicitly clicks Send. The extension does not access any URL automatically or in the background.
permission_justifications.identity: Used only for OAuth 2.0 authorization-code sign-in: when the user clicks "Get new access token", chrome.identity.launchWebAuthFlow opens the provider's sign-in page and returns the authorization code to the extension. The extension never reads the user's Google account or profile, and no identity data leaves the device.
permission_justifications.webRequest: Used to show details the browser hides from the extension's own requests: the redirect chain, Set-Cookie response headers, and the real cause of a network failure (for example a DNS, TLS or refused-connection error). Listeners are limited to the extension's own app tab; no other tab's traffic is observed, and nothing is blocked or modified.
